subject: 2026-11-07-refuter-batch-forge

findings.title: A failed git diff force-removes the worktree with no patch saved
quotes: then it returns a non-empty error and main's `a.txt` is unchanged
findings.fix: on a diff failure, have the caller keep the worktree, and report the worktree path rather than a patch path. An alternative is to return a distinct cause that the caller doesn't treat as "doesn't apply".

sources.situation: the claim commit `since` is gone (AC-2's `"0"*40`), or git fails for another reason. `land` returns `("", {}, "fatal: ...")` before `path.write_bytes(diff)` runs, so no patch file exists. The caller at implement.py:753 sees `err`, runs `git worktree remove --force` on the tree and prints "its changes are in " followed by an empty path. The worker's edits are deleted with nothing to recover them from. Main's `a.txt` is untouched, as AC-2 asks, but the task's work is lost without notice.

a wave task reaches green and `git diff --cached --binary` fails in its worktree. `land` returns patch `""` with an error. The caller (implement.py:754-759) then runs `git worktree remove --force` on the tree and writes "its changes are in " with an empty path. The task's edits existed only in that worktree, so they are lost. D-261106-uom5 says a blocked task's changes go to `T-n.patch`.

findings.reason: src/nio/implement.py:369-371 returns `("", {}, err)` when `git diff --cached --binary` exits non-zero, before `path.write_bytes(diff)` at :373, so no `T-n.patch` exists. The caller at :752-759 treats any `err` the same: it runs `git worktree remove --force` on the tree (which holds the task's only copy of the edits, staged but uncommitted) and prints "its changes are in " with the empty `patch`. Nothing else in the code or spec keeps the tree or names it on this path, so the work is lost.
findings.where: src/nio/implement.py (land's diff-failure return and its caller in green)

findings.title: land still ignores errors from git add and the name-only diff
quotes: `land` returns an empty error and main's `a.txt` matches the tree's
findings.fix: run both git calls with `full=True` and return git's error when either exits non-zero, as the `--binary` diff now does

sources.situation: `git add -A` fails in the worktree (a leftover `.git/index.lock`, or an unreadable file). Its error is discarded. The cached diff then compares the stale index with `since`, which can be empty, and exits 0. Then `names` is empty, so no apply runs and `land` returns an empty error. The task commits and its worktree is removed, but main's `a.txt` was never changed. A failing `--name-only` diff ends the same way, because `records.git` without `full` returns `[]`.

findings.title: A byte-identical refuter answer to a new batch is never read
quotes: answered: a later change to the file has no batch until the next one prints
findings.fix: when a batch is printed, drop the run's refuter sha from `collected` (or delete or rename the old refuter file), so the next answer is always read

sources.situation: the refuter once answered a batch holding only J-1 with `### J-1 / result: confirmed / reason: R`. An escalation juror re-raises J-1, so J-1 is pending again and is re-asked (AC-6). The refuter then writes exactly the same bytes. The sha matches `led["collected"]`, so the file is skipped and nothing says so. J-1 stays pending, and every `nio jury next` prints the same batch again with no hint about why.

J-1 was confirmed from a file holding `### J-1 / result: confirmed / reason: yes`. AC-6 then sends J-1 back to pending and into a new batch. If the refuter answers with the same text, the sha matches the collected one, so nothing is applied. J-1 stays pending and every step prints the same batch again.

findings.title: A forged refuter file is still accepted while a batch is outstanding
quotes: then the collect is refused and J-1 is not refuted
findings.fix: before applying a refuter file, check that it was written after the latest refuter pack (an mtime or nonce in the pack, echoed by the refuter), or have the refuter write to a path no lens juror's pack names

sources.situation: a step collects `spec-testability-2`, which re-raises J-1. J-1 becomes pending and the printed batch sets `asked[run] = [J-1]`. A juror from the same run is still writing, for example a needs-more retry or the slower `spec-testability-3`. It overwrites `spec-refuter.md` with `### J-1 / result: refuted` before the real refuter answers. The next collect finds `asked` holding J-1 and accepts the forgery, so J-1 is refuted. The fix closes only the window when no batch is outstanding.

findings.title: AC-8's test doesn't check that the returned error is git's own
quotes: then it returns git's error and the main tree is unchanged
findings.fix: also assert that the error carries git's own text, for example `"a.txt" in out[2]` or `"patch" in out[2]`.

sources.situation: `land` falls back to "git apply failed" when stderr is empty. The test asserts only that the error is non-empty, so a regression that dropped git's stderr and always returned the fallback string would still pass.

findings.title: The batch check passes on the stale pack from the first batch
quotes: return set(re.findall(r"^### (J-\d+)", batch.read_text(), re.M)) if batch.exists() else set()
findings.fix: delete or read the pack's mtime/content before the step under test, or assert on the step's `next: run nio-refuter` line

sources.situation: in confirmed_then_escalated, the first step already wrote packs/refuter.md listing J-1 and J-2. The confirming step prints no batch and leaves that file in place. So `assert "J-1" in batch_ids(root, run)` holds even if the step after escalation prints no new batch. Only the `pending` assert really checks AC-6's "the printed batch lists J-1".
